phases.name: Set client entry and scope
phases.description: Establish clients, global entry, and the boundary between cacheable public assets and personalized requests.

phases.name: Make canonical social and post writes
phases.description: Validate identity and writes, persist canonical state, and publish durable events for asynchronous work.

phases.name: Distribute posts and build the timeline
phases.description: Materialize ordinary feed candidates, keep read and write paths separate, and bound work for high-follower authors.

phases.name: Process engagement, trends, and search
phases.description: Accept idempotent interactions and update derived counters, hashtag trends, and search indexes asynchronously.

phases.name: Deliver live hints and handle load
phases.description: Notify clients to refresh, observe asynchronous lag, and review global placement and recovery tradeoffs.

steps.phase: Set client entry and scope
steps.title: Keep the brief and unknowns visible
steps.content: The brief requires short posts, follow changes, timelines, likes and retweets, hashtag trends, search, millions of tweets per day, and live feed updates. Treat 280 characters as the maximum accepted post length and apply one consistent Unicode and URL counting rule at API validation. The brief gives no request rate, latency objective, retention period, region topology, or consistency target. Keep these as review questions; do not derive a fabricated capacity or latency target from the daily-volume statement.

steps.phase: Set client entry and scope
steps.title: Add the web client
steps.content: The browser client submits posts and follow actions through the API and reads timeline, search, engagement, and trend views. It treats live messages as refresh hints and fetches authoritative pages through the read API.

component.label: Twitter Web Client
component.description: Browser experience for posting and reading

properties.purpose: Submit validated post, follow, and engagement commands through the API; read cursor-based timelines, search, and trends; treat live messages as refresh hints and fetch canonical content from the read path.

component.highlightReason: The existing Web App catalog component represents the browser client.

steps.phase: Set client entry and scope
steps.title: Add the mobile client
steps.content: Keep mobile behavior on the same authenticated API contracts. Reconnects resume from a feed cursor so a missed push hint does not become a missing post.

component.label: Twitter Mobile Client
component.description: Mobile experience for posting and reading

properties.purpose: Use the shared authenticated API for posts, follows, timelines, search, and engagement; reconnect with a feed cursor and refresh canonical data after a missed live hint.

component.highlightReason: The existing Mobile App catalog component covers the second client surface without adding a custom node.

steps.phase: Set client entry and scope
steps.title: Deliver public assets at the edge
steps.content: Use edge delivery for public application assets. Personalized timelines, authenticated APIs, and private user data must bypass shared edge caching.

component.label: Public Asset CDN
component.description: Global delivery for cacheable public assets

properties.purpose: Serve public application assets close to a global user base. Bypass authenticated APIs, personalized timelines, and private content so shared edge caching cannot expose another user's data.

component.highlightReason: The existing CDN catalog component represents global public-asset delivery.

steps.phase: Set client entry and scope
steps.title: Route requests to healthy service deployments
steps.content: Place a routing layer before the API. It can direct clients toward a healthy nearby deployment, while the actual region topology and cross-region write policy remain decisions for the system's availability and consistency requirements.

component.label: Global API Router
component.description: Route clients to healthy API deployments

properties.purpose: Route client requests to healthy API deployments and support a geographically distributed user base. Keep region placement, failover write ownership, and cross-region consistency explicit review decisions.

component.highlightReason: The existing load balancer catalog component supplies routing without assuming a specific region count.

steps.phase: Set client entry and scope
steps.title: Separate API paths at the gateway
steps.content: Validate and authenticate requests, then route writes, timeline reads, engagement, search, and trend queries to separate service paths. Apply request controls without inventing an unsupported throughput target.

component.label: Social API Gateway
component.description: Authenticated entry and request routing

properties.purpose: Authenticate and validate client requests, enforce account-level access and abuse controls, and route post writes separately from timeline, engagement, search, and trend reads.

component.highlightReason: The existing API Gateway catalog component represents the shared request boundary.

steps.phase: Set client entry and scope
steps.title: Connect edge delivery to the web client
steps.content: Return public application assets through the CDN. Keep user-specific responses on the authenticated API route.

connection.label: Public assets
connection.description: Cacheable application assets only; personalized and authenticated data bypasses the CDN.

steps.phase: Set client entry and scope
steps.title: Route web API traffic
steps.content: Send browser API requests through the global router before they reach the gateway.

connection.label: Web API requests
connection.description: Client requests are routed to a healthy service deployment.

steps.phase: Set client entry and scope
steps.title: Route mobile API traffic
steps.content: Use the same regional routing and API boundary for mobile requests.

connection.label: Mobile API requests
connection.description: Mobile clients use the shared API entry and routing policy.

steps.phase: Set client entry and scope
steps.title: Connect routing to the gateway
steps.content: The gateway is the single policy boundary for authenticated dynamic requests; the CDN does not serve personalized feed data.

connection.label: Routed API traffic
connection.description: Forward dynamic requests to the authenticated API boundary.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Add identity and authorization
steps.content: Authenticate account sessions and provide the actor identity used by post, follow, like, and retweet authorization checks.

component.label: Identity Service
component.description: Account identity and session validation

properties.purpose: Validate account sessions and service identity, return the authenticated actor, and support authorization checks before post, follow, like, and retweet mutations.

component.highlightReason: The existing Auth Service catalog component covers identity without a custom component.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Add the social graph service
steps.content: Make follow and unfollow explicit idempotent commands. Commit each canonical relationship change with a versioned outbox record in the same transaction; publish it asynchronously so feed materialization can catch up without losing a change after a service crash.

component.label: Social Graph Service
component.description: Follow state and relationship changes

properties.purpose: Apply idempotent follow and unfollow commands to canonical relationship state, write a versioned outbox record in the same transaction, and answer follower and following lookups.

component.highlightReason: The existing Backend Server catalog component can represent this domain service.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Persist the relationship graph
steps.content: Keep the current follower relationship queryable by the social service and by feed authorization checks. Choose the physical partitioning after the access pattern and consistency needs are confirmed.

component.label: Follow Graph Store
component.description: Canonical follower and following relationships

properties.purpose: Persist canonical follower and following relationships plus a transactional outbox record in the same transaction for each mutation. Support fan-out recipient lookup and current follow-state checks; select partitioning from measured access patterns.

component.highlightReason: The existing Database catalog component represents durable graph state.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Add the post write service
steps.content: Validate the 280-character maximum on the server using the same counting rule exposed to clients. Reject invalid posts clearly, then commit accepted canonical content and its outbox event together; publish the event asynchronously from that durable record.

component.label: Tweet Write Service
component.description: Validate and persist canonical tweets

properties.purpose: Validate the maximum 280-character post length with a documented Unicode and URL counting rule, authorize the author, and commit canonical tweet content with a transactional outbox event on the write path before acknowledging the write.

component.highlightReason: The existing Backend Server catalog component represents the write path; validation semantics are stated in the service purpose.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Store canonical tweets
steps.content: This store is the source of truth for tweet bodies and author metadata. Commit each post's outbox record in the same transaction; feed and search indexes hold references or projections, not the only copy of canonical content.

component.label: Tweet Store
component.description: Canonical tweet content and author metadata

properties.purpose: Persist canonical tweet identifiers, author, validated body, creation metadata, and a transactional outbox record in the same transaction. Timeline and search projections reference this source so cache or index loss can be repaired.

component.highlightReason: The existing Database catalog component represents canonical durable post storage.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Add the asynchronous event broker
steps.content: Carry committed post, relationship, and engagement events to independent consumers. Queueing prevents feed fan-out and derived indexing from blocking the canonical write response.

component.label: Social Event Broker
component.description: Durable asynchronous event distribution

properties.purpose: Distribute committed post, follow, engagement, and feed-ready events to independent consumers with replayable delivery. Keep asynchronous fan-out and derived work off the canonical request path.

component.highlightReason: The existing Message Broker catalog component matches the brief's queue hint.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Validate identity before mutations
steps.content: Resolve the caller before routing a write so each service can authorize the requested account action.

connection.label: Identity check
connection.description: Authenticate the caller and provide actor context to mutation services.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Route follow commands
steps.content: Send follow and unfollow commands to the service that owns canonical relationship state.

connection.label: Follow API
connection.description: Create or remove an authorized follower relationship idempotently.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Read and update follow state
steps.content: Use the graph store for canonical relationship changes and follower or following lookups.

connection.label: Canonical relationship state
connection.description: Persist follow edges and serve current follower and following queries.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Route post creation
steps.content: Keep post validation and persistence on the write service, distinct from timeline reads.

connection.label: Post write API
connection.description: Route validated post commands to the canonical write path.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Commit the canonical post
steps.content: The write service acknowledges only after the canonical post and its outbox event are durably committed together; retries must not create a second logical post when the client repeats a command.

connection.label: Canonical tweet write
connection.description: Persist validated tweet body, author, creation metadata, and its outbox event atomically.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Publish committed post outbox events
steps.content: A change stream or retryable outbox relay publishes committed creation records at least once. This closes the crash window between storing a post and publishing its event; consumers deduplicate by event ID without holding open the user's post request.

connection.label: Tweet outbox events
connection.description: CDC or an outbox relay forwards committed post events at least once; consumers deduplicate by event ID.

steps.phase: Make canonical social and post writes
steps.title: Publish relationship outbox events
steps.content: Publish the versioned follow change from its committed outbox record. Feed projections can catch up or rebuild, while canonical graph state remains the authority for who follows whom.

connection.label: Follow outbox events
connection.description: CDC or an outbox relay forwards committed, versioned relationship events at least once; consumers deduplicate by event ID.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Add the feed fan-out workers
steps.content: Consume committed posts and relationship changes, resolve recipients, and materialize timeline candidates asynchronously. Make delivery idempotent so broker retries do not duplicate a reader's post.

component.label: Timeline Fan-out Workers
component.description: Asynchronous follower delivery and materialization

properties.purpose: Consume committed tweet and follow events, resolve eligible followers, and idempotently materialize candidate IDs. Keep high-follower authors on a pull path when measured fan-out cost would make push work excessive.

component.highlightReason: The existing Processing Worker catalog component represents the fan-out service named in the brief.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Persist materialized timeline candidates
steps.content: Store candidate tweet identifiers for feed assembly. Current tweet visibility and follow state are checked by the read path, so this projection can be rebuilt and does not grant access by itself.

component.label: Timeline Candidate Store
component.description: Rebuildable per-reader feed candidate identifiers

properties.purpose: Persist rebuildable per-reader candidate tweet identifiers and ordering metadata. Treat entries as hints only; the read service hydrates canonical tweets and checks current visibility and relationship state.

component.highlightReason: The existing Database catalog component can represent a durable materialized timeline projection.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Cache hot timeline data
steps.content: Use Redis to accelerate timeline reads and trend retrieval, while keeping durable source data and freshness behavior explicit. A cache miss or eviction must have a defined store fallback.

component.label: Timeline Read Cache
component.description: Redis cache for hot feed candidates

properties.purpose: Cache hot per-reader timeline candidate identifiers and freshness metadata in Redis. Fall back to the durable candidate store and canonical tweet store on a miss; never treat cached data as current authorization.

component.highlightReason: The existing Cache catalog component supports Redis through its engine property.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Add the timeline read service
steps.content: Serve cursor-based feeds independently of post writes. Merge materialized candidates with pull-based author timelines, hydrate canonical posts, and return a verified page even when optional personalization is unavailable.

component.label: Timeline Read Service
component.description: Assemble and authorize cursor-based feeds

properties.purpose: Serve cursor-based feed reads on an independent read path, separately from the post write path; merge cached and durable candidates with pull-based author timelines, hydrate canonical tweets, check current visibility and follow state, and use bounded fallbacks when a cache or optional ranking dependency is unavailable.

component.highlightReason: The existing Backend Server catalog component represents the latency-sensitive read path.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Feed committed events to fan-out
steps.content: Start feed distribution only from committed events, so a failed post write cannot create a visible timeline candidate.

connection.label: Post and follow events
connection.description: Replayable committed events drive asynchronous timeline materialization.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Resolve current followers
steps.content: Use canonical follower state to select recipients. Feed projections must react to follow and unfollow changes but must not replace the social graph as the source of truth.

connection.label: Follower lookup
connection.description: Resolve current eligible recipients from canonical relationship state.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Write durable feed candidates
steps.content: Persist candidate identifiers idempotently so retries and replays do not create duplicate feed entries.

connection.label: Materialized candidates
connection.description: Idempotent per-reader candidate writes with ordering metadata.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Warm the timeline cache
steps.content: Update or invalidate hot cache entries from the asynchronous path; the durable candidate store remains the rebuild source.

connection.label: Feed cache update
connection.description: Refresh hot candidates or invalidate stale cache entries after materialization.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Signal that a feed candidate is ready
steps.content: Publish a lightweight readiness hint after materialization. This event allows connected clients to refresh without making push delivery the source of feed truth.

connection.label: Feed candidate ready
connection.description: A lightweight event for live delivery; clients still fetch the canonical timeline.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Route feed reads separately
steps.content: Route timeline reads to the read service so high read throughput can scale independently from post validation and persistence.

connection.label: Timeline read API
connection.description: Independent cursor-based feed read path.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Read hot candidates from Redis
steps.content: Use the cache for hot feed candidates and freshness hints; a miss falls through to durable candidates rather than silently returning an empty feed.

connection.label: Hot feed candidates
connection.description: Read cached IDs and freshness state with a durable fallback.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Fall back to durable candidates
steps.content: Fetch the stored candidate page when cache data is absent or stale, then hydrate and authorize each returned post.

connection.label: Durable feed candidates
connection.description: Cursor-based fallback and candidate repair source.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Hydrate canonical tweet content
steps.content: Resolve candidate identifiers against the canonical tweet store. Do not serve a stale cached body or rely on the projection as the only copy.

connection.label: Canonical post hydration
connection.description: Load current tweet bodies and author metadata for feed candidates.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Check current relationship state
steps.content: Apply the latest follow and visibility state during feed assembly so delayed fan-out or a stale cache cannot preserve removed access.

connection.label: Current relationship check
connection.description: Validate current follow state while assembling the personalized timeline.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Choose push and pull by observed fan-out cost
steps.content: Do not fan out every post to every follower. Push ordinary posts when materialization cost is acceptable; pull high-follower authors during feed reads when push amplification would harm freshness or write capacity. Set the transition policy from observed queue lag and read behavior rather than an invented follower cutoff.

decision.question: How should the system handle an author whose post would create excessive fan-out work?
decision.chosen: Use a measured hybrid: push ordinary posts and pull high-follower author timelines during reads.
decision.chosenReason: This keeps common feed reads materialized while avoiding an unbounded write burst for viral authors; the policy can be tuned from observed fan-out and read costs.

alternatives.option: Push every post to every follower
alternatives.tradeoff: A viral author can create a large write burst and delay unrelated feed updates.

alternatives.option: Pull every followed author's posts on every read
alternatives.tradeoff: Timeline reads perform more variable work and can become slow for users who follow many authors.

properties.purpose: Consume committed tweet and follow events; idempotently materialize candidates for ordinary posts and use a pull path for high-follower authors when observed push amplification harms freshness or capacity. Tune the transition policy from queue lag and read behavior, not an assumed follower cutoff.

steps.phase: Distribute posts and build the timeline
steps.title: Keep the read path authoritative
steps.content: Redis and the durable timeline store are projections that accelerate assembly; the canonical tweet and current relationship state determine what the reader may see. If an authorization lookup cannot be confirmed, omit that candidate and let the client retry or continue with other verified entries.

steps.phase: Process engagement, trends, and search
steps.title: Add the engagement service
steps.content: Accept likes and retweets as idempotent user-to-tweet actions. Commit each interaction with an outbox record so accepted actions reach asynchronous consumers even if the service stops immediately after the database write; keep viral-post counters off the synchronous path.

component.label: Engagement Service
component.description: Like and retweet commands with idempotent writes

properties.purpose: Authorize and idempotently record likes and retweets per user and tweet. Commit each interaction with a transactional outbox record so viral activity can feed asynchronous aggregates without serializing on a hot counter.

component.highlightReason: The existing Backend Server catalog component represents interaction logic.

steps.phase: Process engagement, trends, and search
steps.title: Persist interaction identity
steps.content: Store the user's interaction state, uniqueness key, and outbox record in the same transaction. Derived counts can lag briefly and be recomputed from accepted events.

component.label: Engagement Store
component.description: Durable likes, retweets, and deduplication state

properties.purpose: Persist per-user like and retweet state with uniqueness that makes retries idempotent, plus a transactional outbox record in the same transaction. Keep derived totals rebuildable from accepted interaction events instead of synchronously contending on one viral-post counter.

component.highlightReason: The existing Database catalog component represents durable interaction records.

steps.phase: Process engagement, trends, and search
steps.title: Add real-time trend processing
steps.content: Consume tweet and engagement events, extract hashtags, update configured trend windows, and publish a freshness marker. This derived view is eventually consistent with accepted source events.

component.label: Hashtag Trend Processor
component.description: Streaming hashtag aggregation

properties.purpose: Consume committed tweet and engagement events, extract hashtags, maintain configured trend windows, and publish an eventually consistent result with freshness information. Rebuild derived state by replaying retained source events when needed.

component.highlightReason: The existing Stream Processor catalog component represents the real-time aggregation concept.

steps.phase: Process engagement, trends, and search
steps.title: Cache trending topics in Redis
steps.content: Serve the current materialized hashtag view from Redis. Make its freshness visible and refresh it from the stream processor rather than calculating trends on each user request.

component.label: Trending Topics Cache
component.description: Redis view of current hashtag trends

properties.purpose: Serve the latest materialized hashtag trends from Redis with freshness metadata. Refresh asynchronously from the stream processor so trend aggregation does not run on the request path.

component.highlightReason: Redis is both named in the brief and supported by the existing Cache catalog engine options.

steps.phase: Process engagement, trends, and search
steps.title: Add the search read service
steps.content: Accept searches for tweets and users, query an index, then resolve results through canonical data and current visibility checks. Index freshness is not a promise of immediate consistency.

component.label: Tweet and User Search API

properties.purpose: Validate tweet and user search requests, query the search index, hydrate canonical results, and apply current visibility rules before returning indexed matches that may be slightly stale.

component.highlightReason: The existing Backend Server catalog component represents the query API separately from its index.

steps.phase: Process engagement, trends, and search
steps.title: Add the asynchronous search indexer
steps.content: Consume committed post and user-profile events and update searchable projections independently from the write response. Reprocessing an event should converge rather than create duplicate documents.

component.label: Search Indexer
component.description: Asynchronous tweet and user indexing

properties.purpose: Consume committed tweet and user-profile events, idempotently update search documents, and keep indexing latency outside the user's canonical write path.

component.highlightReason: The existing Processing Worker catalog component represents asynchronous index maintenance.

steps.phase: Process engagement, trends, and search
steps.title: Add the search index
steps.content: Index tweet text and searchable user fields for query retrieval. Treat the index as a rebuildable projection, not the authority for post existence or visibility.

component.label: Tweet and User Search Index
component.description: Full-text index for posts and user profiles

component.highlightReason: The existing Search Engine catalog component directly represents full-text indexing.

steps.title: Route like and retweet commands
steps.content: Keep engagement mutations independent from feed assembly and search reads.

steps.title: Persist idempotent interactions

steps.title: Publish interaction outbox events

steps.title: Query the search projection

steps.title: Index committed content asynchronously

steps.phase: Deliver live hints and handle load

steps.phase: Deliver live hints and handle load
steps.title: Review global placement and consistency
steps.content: The router and CDN provide a global entry and public-asset delivery pattern, but the brief does not define data residency, regional failover, write ownership, or cross-region consistency. Choose those with product availability and consistency requirements; do not imply that an edge cache makes personalized reads globally consistent.

steps.phase: Deliver live hints and handle load
steps.title: Scale fan-out from observed lag
steps.content: Watch consumer lag, oldest-event age, duplicate rates, and feed freshness. Add or rebalance consumers while preserving idempotency and per-key ordering; isolate poison events for inspection and replay. Do not slow canonical post acceptance just because derived feeds are behind.

scaleTrigger.metric: Consumer lag, oldest-event age, duplicate rate, and feed freshness
scaleTrigger.action: Scale or rebalance consumers, preserve idempotent writes and ordering, and inspect then replay poison events
scaleTrigger.impact: Restores derived-feed freshness while keeping accepted post writes independent from fan-out recovery.

steps.phase: Deliver live hints and handle load
steps.title: Scale trend processing from freshness
steps.content: When trend freshness degrades, inspect event lag and processing failures, then scale or replay the stream processor. Keep the cached response marked with its freshness rather than presenting stale aggregates as current.

scaleTrigger.metric: Trend event lag, processing failures, and published freshness marker
scaleTrigger.action: Scale consumers or replay source events and refresh the Redis materialized view
scaleTrigger.impact: Recovers real-time trend processing while exposing eventual consistency to readers.

steps.phase: Deliver live hints and handle load
steps.title: Define retry and recovery behavior
steps.content: Use idempotent consumers because queue delivery may repeat. Recover missing feed hints by reading from the saved cursor; recover cache loss from durable candidate and canonical stores; rebuild search and trend projections from their event sources. Derived views may lag, but canonical post and relationship state remains authoritative.

steps.phase: Deliver live hints and handle load
steps.title: Trace the complete product flow
steps.content: A post is validated and committed before its event is queued; fan-out materializes ordinary feed candidates while high-follower authors can be pulled during reads; the timeline service hydrates canonical posts and checks current relationships. Likes and retweets persist idempotently, then update counts and trends asynchronously. Search indexes tweets and users from events. Feed-ready hints prompt clients to fetch the canonical feed.
